summary: Google DeepMind released Nano Banana 2 Lite (a faster, cheaper Gemini image model) and made Gemini Omni Flash (a video generation and conversational editing model) available to developers via Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and consumer surfaces.

mechanisms.reason: The new Lite image model is explicitly priced and positioned as cheaper and faster than its predecessor, indicating reduced compute/cost per generated image.
mechanisms.quote: Cost-efficiency ($0.034 per 1K image): A cost-efficient choice for developers focused on drafting, ideating, managing operational budgets or low-bandwidth usage.

mechanisms.reason: The models are rolled out broadly across many consumer and developer surfaces, expanding the number of contexts generating inference calls.
mechanisms.quote: It is also rolling out today in Google consumer surfaces including AI Mode in Search, Gemini app and many other products .

practices.reason: Developers can swap the legacy Nano Banana model for the Lite version to get stated gains in speed, cost and image quality, and gain new video generation capability via Omni Flash.
practices.quote: It’s our recommended replacement for developers currently using our first version of Nano Banana (gemini-2.5-flash-image), you can swap it out now for immediate benefits across key performance dimensions.

practices.reason: The document describes a concrete chaining pattern -- generating an image with Nano Banana 2 Lite then animating it with Omni Flash via the Interactions API -- with a stated multi-turn edit limit engineers can implement directly.
practices.quote: by using the Interactions API for these multi-turn experiences, you can maintain session history and context so users can stack up to three sequential edits.

practices.reason: A benchmark comparison against competitor models is shown but methodology and test set are not detailed enough to reproduce.
practices.quote: Performance benchmarks for Nano Banana 2 and 2 Lite compared to competitor AI image models, evaluating trade-offs between generation/editing quality (Elo scores), processing latency and cost per 1K-resolution image.

practices.reason: Teams using the legacy Nano Banana model are pointed toward a recommended replacement, creating a migration consideration though no hard deprecation date is given.
practices.quote: We recommend upgrading to Nano Banana 2 Lite for better quality, faster speeds and lower costs.
